newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Rockets injure Israeli woman, damage synagogue.
newsitem.headline: Rockets injure Israeli woman, damage synagogue.

text.p: Katyusha rockets fired by guerrillas in Lebanon slammed into a northern Israeli town early on Friday, slightly injuring a woman and damaging a synagogue, the military said.

Witnesses said it was the first time the rockets had landed in Kiryat Shmona, the largest town in Israel's Upper Galilee, in the more than 15 months since Israel and Hizbollah guerrillas undertook not to fire on civilian targets.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack just after dawn on the town of 22,000 people. Hizbollah, an Iranian-backed Islamic militant group, had threatened this week to carry out attacks inside Israel.
Cross-border violence has intensified in recent days. On Thursday five Lebanese were killed by two bombs and Israeli shelling.
Since Monday 13 people have died in the bloodshed -- including seven civilians -- starting with an Israeli commando raid in which five Hizbollah guerrillas were killed with a roadside bomb.

Avraham Aderi of Kiryat Shmona said he was drinking tea with other residents after morning prayers when the Katyusha slammed into the town, damaging the synagogue. He called it a miracle none of them was hurt.
Hizbollah is fighting to drive the Israelis and their local Lebanese militia allies from Israel's 15-km (nine-mile) occupation zone in south Lebanon.
Israel set up the zone -- a site of frequent rocket attacks, clashes and bombs -- to protect its northern settlements from the Katyushas.

Israel and Hizbollah reached an understanding not to attack civilian targets as part of a 1996 ceasefire that ended a 17-day Israeli onslaught in which about 200 people, mainly Lebanese civilians, were killed.
